intro: AI engineer interviews ask how I'd build, debug and measure LLM products: RAG that gives wrong answers, evals, agents versus workflows, cost and latency, prompt injection. So I learn top-down, starting from what I already use at work and going one layer down each week.

spine.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
spine.note: About 3.5 hours, watched once over four sittings.

spine.title: AI Engineering
spine.note: Read in order, one chapter section per session.

spine.title: Search over my study notes
spine.note: Grows every month and is measured with a test set.

path.learn: Karpathy's deep dive + AI Engineering ch. 1
path.build: A Python script that calls an LLM and counts tokens and cost on my own chats
path.question: What is a token, and why does a longer context cost more and run slower?

path.learn: Ch. 2: how models pick words, structured output
path.build: Make the LLM return strict JSON, with retries when it breaks
path.question: How do you make LLM output reliable?

path.build: Embed my notes; search with plain numpy first, then pgvector
path.question: Walk me through a RAG pipeline.

path.build: 30 test questions; measure how often the right note is in the top 5; try chunk sizes, keyword + vector search, a reranker
path.question: The answer is wrong but the document exists. Where's the bug?

path.build: README with my numbers, and one X thread
path.question: Tell me about something you built and how you know it works.

skipped.why: It trains data-science skills (tabular models, competitions). That's a different job from building LLM products.
Useful depth, but rarely asked for AI engineer roles. It moves to phase 2 as optional.
